mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) has a negative correlation with S&P 500 20-day returns, meaning that as FEDFUNDS decreases, returns increase due to reduced discount rates in equity valuation models. This relationship is consistent across historical data and is not contingent on additional conditions.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS and S&P 500 20-day returns is positive (correlation coefficient > 0) over the 10-year historical data.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls to 0.5% or below, it signals an aggressive monetary easing cycle that reduces discount rates and stimulates equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% over the 10-year historical data.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.5%) and a low unemployment rate (UNRATE <= 5.0%) indicates a strong economic expansion with accommodative monetary policy, which predicts positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% AND UNRATE <= 5.0% over the 10-year historical data.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (characterized by high GDP growth and low unemployment), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 2% in one month signals weakening demand and impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST declines > 2% in 1 month and the regime is late-cycle expansion over the 10-year historical data.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO) has a positive correlation with S&P 500 20-day returns, as higher industrial output signals robust economic activity and strong corporate earnings, leading to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO and S&P 500 20-day returns is not positive (correlation coefficient <= 0) over the 10-year historical data.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 102.0, it indicates strong economic growth that supports equity valuations, predicting positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO > 102.0 over the 10-year historical data.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of rising housing starts (HOUST > 1.5% increase in one month) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.0%) signals economic overheating and impending monetary tightening, which predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 1.5% in 1 month AND CPIAUCSL > 2.0%
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST rises > 1.5% in 1 month AND CPIAUCSL > 2.0% over the 10-year historical data.

mechanism_narrative: In a recession risk period (characterized by high unemployment volatility and slowing GDP growth), a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points in three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions and weak economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months and the regime is recession risk period over the 10-year historical data.
